speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; can you tell me exactly how long the bleeding from your wisdom tooth extraction has persisted? Also, have you noticed any unusual bruising or bleeding from other sites like your gums or nose recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall if the bleeding was difficult to stop after other minor injuries or dental procedures in the past? Also, does your uncle's history of joint swelling suggest he experienced bleeding into his joints?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of joint swelling, I suspect hemophilia, so I need to clarify if those joint episodes in your uncle were painful or resulted in limited movement. Also, has this bleeding tendency affected your ability to form clots after minor cuts?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, takes no medications. Social history: The patient is a high school student with no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did your uncle experience painful joint swelling that limited his movement, which would suggest bleeding into the joints? Additionally, do you recall if your own bleeding was difficult to stop after other minor cuts or injuries in the past?

text: The prolonged partial thromboplastin time with normal platelets and family history strongly points to a factor deficiency, likely Hemophilia A or B. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A
